Ultrasonic Sensor Range and HC SR04 Dimensions

What is the range of an ultrasonic sensor? The popular HC SR04 module measures from about 2 cm to 400 cm. Below 2 cm the echo returns before the receiver is ready (blind zone), and beyond about 4 m the echo becomes too weak. Practical, repeatable ultrasonic range indoors is usually 2 cm to 300 cm on a flat, hard target.

ParameterHC SR04 value
Measuring range2 cm to 400 cm
ResolutionAbout 0.3 cm
Beam angleAbout 15°
Frequency40 kHz
Supply5 V DC, about 15 mA
Trigger pulse10 µs HIGH
Module dimensions45 × 20 × 15 mm
Transducer diameterAbout 16 mm each

What Reduces Ultrasonic Sensor Range

  • Soft or angled targets such as cloth, foam or sloped surfaces that scatter the echo.
  • Small targets that are narrower than the beam.
  • Air temperature changes, which change the speed of sound.
  • Noise from motors or other ultrasonic sensors working nearby.

Industrial ultrasonic level transmitters reach much longer ranges, from a few metres up to tens of metres, using bigger transducers and lower frequencies.
